title: Atomic vendor partitioning and distro-aware preflight profiles for air-gapped installs
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds vendor partitioning and distro-specific preflight profiles. Operators can opt into partitioned bundles to reduce airgap bundle sizes and speed up upgrades. Includes helm/terraform helpers and rollback safety checks.
description:
Motivation: air-gapped/private installs at large customers continue to balloon in size because vendor bundles include all distro overlays and optional modules. This PR introduces 'vendor partitioning' — a deterministic layout that splits an offline bundle into: base-runtime, distro-overlay/<distro>, optional-modules/<name>. Partitioning reduces snapshot sizes and allows targeted delta application during upgrades.

What this PR does (single-string summary):
- Adds a partitioner that computes a deterministic, signed index for offline bundles (ordering + checksums).
- Introduces distro-aware preflight profiles that run lightweight probes and kernel/config checks before applying an overlay. Profiles are authored as small YAMLs under installer/preflight/profiles/*.
- Adds an atomic delta-applier that applies partitions in a safe order with checkpoints and idempotent rollback markers.
- Helm chart changes: offline preflight Job, a new hook for staged overlay apply, and a post-install verification hook.
- Terraform module updates: registry seeding helpers (local registry init), a new variable to control partitioned-seeding, and provider validation.
- Rollback tooling: partial-rollback controller that can revert only the last applied partition when a failure is detected, preserving previously applied overlays.

Checklist (for reviewers and operators):
- [x] Unit tests for partitioner checksum and ordering logic.
- [x] End-to-end airgap integration test that seeds a local registry and validates staged apply/rollback.
- [x] Terraform validate + plan tests for the registry module.
- [x] Manual smoke on k3s and RKE2 (see test notes).

Migration notes: existing sealed bundles remain compatible. Operators that opt into partitioning will need to re-generate the offline bundle with `installer tools bundle partition --profile <profile-name>`; the CLI supports a `--compat` flag to emit a single combined bundle for older toolchains. The preflight profiles are additive and won't run unless referenced in the install configuration.

Security notes: the partition index is signed with the existing bundle signing key (same key family used for full-bundles). We added signature verification to the apply path and fail-safe behavior that prevents partial applies if the signature verification fails. Audit logs emit partition-level events for traceability.

Related: ENG-1423 (bundle size reductions), ENG-1429 (safe upgrades), SUP-620 (customer incident that motivated partial rollback).

Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes to the installer control plane. Helm values add an opt-in `partitioning.enabled` boolean. Default remains false to avoid surprising existing customers.

notes_for_operators: To opt-in: regenerate bundles with `installer tools bundle partition --profile rke2 --sign-key /path/to/key` and set helm value `partitioning.enabled=true`. For rollbacks, use `installer rollback --partial last-partition` which will attempt a safe revert of the last applied partition and leave previously applied partitions intact. See docs/operator/partitioning.md for full steps.
test_summary: Unit coverage added for partitioner and verifier. E2E airgap job completed in CI: seeded local registry (approx 450MB base, 120MB rke2 overlay, 80MB optional modules) and verified staged apply and partial rollback in <12 minutes on the CI runner. Manual smoke validated on k3s (v1.27) and RKE2 (v1.27) with both partitioning enabled and disabled.
